narrative:
The model determined that you have a 51% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability is just over the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that weighed most heavily in this decision were the status of your checking account, your credit history, and the type of property you own. Your checking account being in negative balance (<0 DM) was the strongest factor pushing the prediction toward bad credit risk. Among approved applicants, only 12.6% have a negative balance, while the majority (59.2%) have no checking account at all. This placed you in a higher-risk category from the start.

Your credit history of “no credits or all paid” was the second most important driver and also increased the likelihood of being seen as a bad risk. This category is quite rare among approved applicants (only 1%), whereas most have a history of existing credits that were paid on time (57.3%).

The one positive element was that you own real estate. This factor worked in your favor and pulled the prediction somewhat toward approval, but unfortunately it was not strong enough to overcome the concerns raised by your account status and credit history.

You should focus on building a positive credit history over the next 12–18 months and aim to bring your checking account balance into positive territory. Once these areas improve, reapply. Many applicants in similar situations become eligible after demonstrating consistent financial responsibility.
